newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finance assoc. says more suspensions unlikely.
newsitem.headline: Thai finance assoc. says more suspensions unlikely.

text.p: The Thai Association of Finance Companies said it welcomed the central bank's decision on Friday to cut the number of firms in the crowded sector through mergers but said it did not anticipate more suspensions of company operations.

"The central bank's move should cover all troubles of finance firms. I don't think there will be any more suspension of finance firms," Bantherng Thantivit, the group's president, told a news conference.
The Bank of Thailand suspended the operations of 16 weak listed and unlisted finance companies for 30 days on Friday.

It gave them 14 days to come up with plans to merge or face having their business licences revoked. In that case, they would be absorbed by healthier firms under a purchase and assumption arrangement.
"The goverment move today was in the right direction to reduce the number of finance companies in the crowded finance sector," Bantherng said.

"In future, the number of finance companies will be reduced and the remaining ones will be stronger and can do a wider range of financial services. It is a good measure to restructure the sector," he added.

Thailand's ailing finance firms have been hit by a liquidity crunch and overexposure to the depressed property sector. The current economic downturn, the worst in over a decade, has further worsened their positions, analysts said.

Bantherng said he expected that there would be some withdrawals of deposits from the same finance firms as a result of concerns about the shakeout. "But the situation will normalise very quickly once people understand the rationale behind the suspension," he added.
